inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments' $23m (2024: $27m); no separate equity-award tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in kpis); EBT share purchases ($36m) are the settlement mechanism and sit in buyback_cash, not SBC
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing outflow is $36m of EBT purchases only. A separate $250m on-market buyback was announced 26 Feb 2026 for execution during 2026; $227m spent by 5 Aug 2026. The flat share count is therefore funded in 2026, and the shares bought in H1 2026 are already removed from shares_outstanding (see share_count_basis).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are USD (Hikma reports in US dollars; LSE quote is GBp, pence). Per-share values computed in USD then converted at GBPUSD 1.3233 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09T21:29Z): 1 USD = 100/1.3233 = 75.57 GBp. Parity check: HIK.L 1612p x 1.3233 / 100 = $21.33 vs OTC ADR HKMPY $42.39 (2 ADR = 1 share, 2026-10-09) = $21.20 per share, a 0.6% tie, and HKMPF $21.06 (2026-10-08). refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive fx_rate when GBPUSD moves more than ~2%.
inputs.share_count_basis: ESTIMATED fully diluted at 30 June 2026. Shares in free issue at 31 Dec 2025 were 220,106,915 (234,719,686 issued less 12,833,233 treasury less 1,779,538 EBT; FY2025 AR note 29). The $250m buyback announced 26 Feb 2026 had spent $227m by 5 Aug 2026; pro-rating to 30 June gives ~$180m at the Feb-Jun average price of 1,373p / GBPUSD 1.3404 = $18.41, i.e. ~9.8m shares, leaving ~210.3m in free issue. Add 2.1m potentially dilutive share awards (FY2025 note 11: 222,684,171 diluted vs 220,587,683 basic) = 212.4m. H1 2026 core EPS 128c on $277m core profit implies a ~216m H1 weighted average, consistent with a ~210m period-end count. The interim statutory report is not in the filing set; replace with the reported 30 June 2026 count when it is extracted. June-30 shares are paired with June-30 net debt so that the buyback cash already spent is charged once. Count held FLAT thereafter because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Company-defined Group net debt at 30 June 2026: total debt $1,957m (borrowings plus lease liabilities) less cash $263m = $1,694m (H1 2026 results presentation slide 12; 1.9x core EBITDA). This already reflects the $111m of FY2025 legal settlements placed in restricted cash at 31 Dec 2025 and paid in January 2026, and ~$180m of 2026 buyback. Contingent consideration liabilities were nil at 31 Dec 2025 ($85m in 2024, $75m paid in 2025).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built WACC. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.8 for a diversified generics/branded pharma with MENA exposure gives cost of equity ~8.2%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (BBB, 2025 Eurobond refinancing, core net finance expense guided $99-103m on ~$1.9bn gross debt); market-value weights ~73/27 give ~7.2%. House uses 8.5% in all three scenarios: the premium over the arithmetic WACC covers the structural US generics price erosion and the single-regulator (FDA) exposure, and is charged once, here, not again in the scenario flows or via per-scenario WACC differences.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Reported OCF/FCF does not deduct lease principal ($11m FY2025, in financing); lease liabilities ($53m at 31 Dec 2025: $45m non-current + $8m current, FY2025 note 15) are inside the company's net debt figure used in the bridge. Ongoing lease-asset renewal (~0.4% of revenue) is folded into capex_pct_path. Nothing is deducted twice: principal stays out of the flows, liabilities stay in net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (NCI profit share $5m FY2025 is immaterial, ~1% of profit); the $13m NCI balance at 31 Dec 2025 is deducted once in equity_bridge. FY0 check: core operating profit $741m less core net finance ~$24m less 21.5% tax = ~$563m vs reported core attributable profit $503m; the gap is core finance costs classified below operating profit plus JV/other, within non-operating noise.
inputs.interest_income_treatment: Interest income received ($6m cash, $11m P&L in FY2025) is NOT stripped: Hikma is a net-debt company ($1.7bn), so there is no cash pile being added to EV that the interest would double-count. The $72m FY2025 finance-income gain from remeasuring contingent consideration is non-cash and excluded from core; it does not enter the base.
inputs.capex_basis: capex_pct_path covers PPE plus purchased intangibles (product rights/licences) plus ~0.4% lease renewal. FY2025: PPE $197m (incl. $22m reimbursed CMO project) + intangibles $120m = $317m, 9.5% of revenue; FY2020-25 average ~8%. Management guides PPE capex of 5-6% of revenue on average ($190-210m for 2026, before reimbursed CMO-partner spend); Bedford comes online 2028, after which PPE intensity eases. Reimbursed CMO capex is excluded (the partner pays). Intangibles purchases have no core D&A counterpart (amortisation of non-software intangibles is excluded from core), so the cash cost is charged through capex with no offsetting add-back: conservative and internally consistent.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is core EBITDA (core operating profit before depreciation and software amortisation, company definition) PLUS the SBC expense that core already deducts, so SBC is then charged once via sbc_pct_path. FY2025: core EBITDA $853m + SBC $23m = $876m = 26.2% of revenue (FY2024: 824+27 = 27.0% of core revenue 3,156). da_pct_path is core D&A only ($112m FY2025 = 3.3%), rising slightly with Bedford depreciation from 2028. Reported (statutory) EBITDA $780m sits below core because of intangible amortisation, impairments, legal settlements and reorganisation charges, none of which are in the component build except through the capex line.
inputs.fcf_base_note: FY2025 reported FCF of $119m (OCF $436m less capex $317m) is a trough: OCF carried $186m of one-off legal settlement payments and capex was a peak. Underlying FY2025 unlevered owner FCF is ~$282m (436+186-317-23). Interest paid ($83m) is in financing under Hikma's IFRS presentation, so reported OCF is already before interest and the flows are unlevered. The engine builds forward FCF from components, so last_fcf is the audit anchor, not the projection base.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (operating company: generics/branded/injectables pharma; routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 2, non-US operating company, with the adaptations file applied for currency (USD flows vs GBp quote), leases (treatment A), NCI (bridge) and risk-charged-once). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. Price is the LSE regular close of 2026-10-09 (not after-hours). Guidance anchors (FY2026, reiterated 6 Aug 2026 with Branded now at the top end): Group revenue +2-4%, core operating profit $720-770m, Injectables low-single-digit growth at 27-28% margin, Branded +6-8% at ~25% margin, Hikma Rx flat at ~20% margin, net finance expense $99-103m, capex $190-210m, core ETR ~23%. Year-1 component build gives EBIT of ~$756m, at the top of the guided range, consistent with H1 2026 core operating profit of $405m (+9%) on an H1-weighted Branded year. SBC-light market: SBC is 0.7% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow but non-zero and band_position is reported.

equity_bridge.note: FY2025 AR consolidated balance sheet, NCI $13m (2024: $11m); flows are consolidated so NCI is deducted once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (FY2020 $2,135m -> FY2025 $2,593m), cross-checked against FY2026 revenue guidance of +2-4% and core EPS 5yr CAGR of 5.7%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 4.0% is 46% below revenue 5yr CAGR 7.4% (buybacks of $375m in 2020 and $303m in 2022 plus dividends shrank the equity base while revenue compounded; revenue also includes the 2024 Xellia acquisition). Reported EPS 5yr CAGR of 0% and 3yr CAGR of 29% are both distorted by the FY2022-23 impairments and legal charges; core EPS (5.7%/7.9%) is the cleaner series.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2020 $213m, FY2021 $380m, FY2022 $283m, FY2023 $379m, FY2024 $302m, FY2025 $96m. The FY2025 endpoint is depressed by $186m of one-off legal settlement cash and peak capex; on the underlying FY2025 figure of ~$282m the 5yr owner-FCF CAGR is +5.8% and the 3yr CAGR ~0%. SBC has been flat at $22-29m (0.7-1.2% of revenue) across the period, so SBC is not eating the growth; working capital (245 days) and capex are.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 at the guided 2-4% midpoint; 4% in FY2027-29 as Tyzavan, the CMO business and MENA Branded (6-8%) outgrow a flat Hikma Rx and a low-single-digit Injectables base; fading to 2.5% terminal.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 core EBITDA+SBC margin of 26.0% reproduces core operating profit of ~$756m, the top of the $720-770m guidance that H1 tracked to; +1pp over five years from Branded mix and Bedford scale, offset by R&D rising to 5-6% of revenue.
base.capex_rationale: 8.5% in FY2026-27 = PPE $200m + intangibles ~$80m + lease renewal; eases to 6.5% once Bedford (online 2028) is built. Partner-reimbursed CMO capex excluded.
base.wc_rationale: Working capital days 245 (receivables and inventory far exceed payables): each $1 of revenue growth consumes ~$0.30 of cash, so capture is negative.

scenario_narratives.base: Hikma delivers its reiterated FY2026 guidance (revenue +2-4%, core operating profit $720-770m, top end after a strong Branded H1) and then compounds at ~4% for three years: Tyzavan replaces Vanco Ready in US Injectables, the contract-manufacturing business (Bedford online 2028) adds steady volume, MENA Branded grows 6-8% on chronic therapies, and Hikma Rx stays flat as sodium oxybate competition offsets differentiated launches. Core margin edges up ~1pp as mix improves and R&D settles at 5-6% of revenue. Capex steps down from the Bedford peak after 2028; working capital (245 days) keeps absorbing ~30c per $1 of growth. Terminal value is bound by the 15x cap, i.e. the model does not assume a re-rating beyond a mid-teens FCF multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: US Injectables returns to mid-single-digit growth as Tyzavan, 505(b)(2) launches and the CMO platform scale through the Bedford capacity; MENA Branded sustains high-single-digit growth with tender share gains and in-licensed partnerships (gEllipta, 10 MENA partnerships); Hikma Rx holds sodium oxybate economics longer than feared. Group grows ~6% through FY2029 with core EBITDA margin expanding to 29% (back toward the 2021 level) as scale, mix and the end of the Bedford build-out lift conversion. Capex normalises to 6% and net debt falls below 1x EBITDA, leaving room for continued buybacks. Terminal growth 3%, cap 15x.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sodium oxybate generic competition arrives faster and deeper, US injectables price erosion resumes as competitors return to products Hikma gained share on, and the Vanco Ready-to-Tyzavan transition loses share rather than holding it; MENA geopolitics disrupts tender timing and in-licensing supply (as it did in H1 2026) and currency devaluations (Egypt, Algeria, Sudan) hit reported Branded revenue; US tariff or MFN drug-pricing policy compresses the injectables segment. Revenue stalls for two years and core margin falls ~3pp to 23% while capex commitments (Bedford, Tunisia, Algeria) are already made and R&D is rising; leverage stays near 2x so buybacks stop. Terminal growth 2%, cap 12x. No going-concern or covenant risk: the balance sheet is BBB and the downside is a de-rating, not solvency.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because two of the named bear axes are already visible in H1 2026 (US Injectables revenue down, sodium oxybate competition increasing into H2, MENA supply disruption) and US drug-pricing/tariff policy is a live single-regulator risk. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right (US Injectables re-acceleration, MENA growth sustained through geopolitics, Rx holding oxybate economics). Base 50%: guidance has been met or tightened upward for two years and the balance sheet is investment grade, so the central case is credible.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Hikma is valued as a cash-generative, moderately leveraged generics and branded pharma company on a strict owner-FCF basis: core EBITDA (plus SBC, charged once) less core D&A, cash tax at the guided 23%, PPE and intangible capex, and a negative working-capital capture, discounted at a USD 8.5% WACC with the terminal value capped at 15x FCF. The flows are unlevered and the June-2026 company-defined net debt (including leases) and NCI are deducted once. Values are computed in USD and converted to pence at the dated GBPUSD rate; the FY2025 reported FCF trough ($186m legal settlements, peak capex) is not carried forward, nor is the FY2025 finance-income gain.
key_risks_to_valuation: Share count is an estimate for 30 June 2026 (buyback pro-rated); a reported interim count could move value per share by ~1-2%.
FX: a 5% move in GBPUSD moves every pence figure ~5% with no change in the USD model; refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate.
US generics pricing, FDA inspection outcomes at Columbus/Cherry Hill/Bedford, and US drug-pricing or tariff policy are the dominant swing factors in the flows.
MENA currency devaluations and geopolitical disruption to tenders and in-licensing supply.
Capex and R&D are both stepping up (Bedford to 2028, R&D to 5-6% of revenue): if the returns lag, FCF conversion stays below the modelled path.
Working-capital intensity (245 days) means growth above the base case consumes cash before it creates value.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, LSE regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1,187-1,865p. FX from Yahoo GBPUSD=X at the date in inputs.fx_note; parity checked against the HKMPY/HKMPF OTC ADRs.
